findings.highlight: The unusual day goes by quickly.
findings.evidenceJa: 慣れない一日は慌ただしく過ぎていった
findings.governingReading: The unaccustomed day passes in a rush.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s lack of familiarity is replaced by an objective claim that the day itself is unusual, while bustle becomes mere speed.

findings.highlight: It’s not like there was any memorable moments nor were it so boring that I regret doing it.
findings.evidenceJa: 印象に残るほど楽しい出来事があった訳ではないし、後悔するほどつまらない時間ではなかった
findings.governingReading: There was nothing memorably enjoyable, but it was not so dull that he regretted it.
findings.explanation: The paired assessment is left grammatically malformed, with number disagreement and an unlicensed it-subject.

findings.highlight: I can be proud of it in the end.
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーをこうして連れ回した事を、俺は最後に誇れる筈だ
findings.governingReading: In the end he should be able to take pride in having taken Saber around like this.
findings.explanation: The concrete basis of Shirou’s pride—giving Saber time outside combat—is reduced to an empty pronoun.

findings.highlight: she has to spend some time not fighting, or there’s no point in her being here
findings.evidenceJa: 戦い以外の時間を重ねなくては彼女がここにいる意味がない
findings.governingReading: Unless they accumulate time together outside battle, there is no meaning in her being here.
findings.explanation: A relational need to build noncombat memories becomes something Saber herself has to do.

findings.highlight: stops. She is watching a mountain of rubble.
findings.evidenceJa: 足を止めて川の中程を見つめていた
findings.governingReading: She stops and looks toward the middle of the river, where the rubble lies.
findings.explanation: The sightline and the rubble’s location in midriver disappear.

findings.highlight: Steel frames and the likes are piled right up to the water surface
findings.evidenceJa: 水面より少し低い程度に積み重なった鉄骨やら何やら
findings.governingReading: Steel frames and other debris are piled to just below the water surface.
findings.explanation: The pile’s top is moved from slightly submerged to level with the surface.

findings.highlight: it seems like a ship sank or something, and pieces of it flowed into a mountain
findings.evidenceJa: ずいぶん昔に停泊していた船が沈没したとかで破片が流れ、溜まって山になったのだそうだ
findings.governingReading: He has heard that fragments from a ship anchored and sunk long ago drifted here and accumulated into a mound.
findings.explanation: The age, anchored state, accumulation process, and layered hearsay are collapsed into an incoherent image of fragments flowing into a mountain.

findings.highlight: I have to take care to only use Excalibur in an open place like this.
findings.evidenceJa: エクスカリバーを使う時は、せめてこれぐらい広いところじゃないとシャレにならない
findings.governingReading: When Excalibur is used, it needs at least this much open space or the consequences are no joke.
findings.explanation: The English explicitly makes Shirou the user of Excalibur, contradicting the Servant and weapon relation.

findings.highlight: I think Kiritsugu knew how the battle would turn out.
findings.evidenceJa: 切嗣には戦いの流れが読めていたのでしょう
findings.governingReading: Saber supposes Kiritsugu could read how the battle was developing.
findings.explanation: Tactical anticipation is promoted into knowledge of the battle’s eventual outcome.

findings.highlight: Saber looks down at the river yearningly.
findings.evidenceJa: 懐かしそうにセイバーは川を見下ろした
findings.governingReading: Saber looks down at the river with nostalgia.
findings.explanation: Recollection of a past shared with Kiritsugu becomes present longing.

findings.highlight: She gasps.
findings.evidenceJa: 息を呑む
findings.governingReading: Shirou catches his breath.
findings.explanation: The unmarked first-person narration is assigned to Saber, transferring the anxious reaction to the person being questioned.

findings.highlight: Saber opens her eyes in amazement.
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーはきょとん、と目を開いた
findings.governingReading: Saber opens her eyes with a blank, puzzled look.
findings.explanation: Her uncomprehending surprise becomes stronger amazement.

findings.highlight: a voice of hope
findings.evidenceJa: 憧れを含んだ声
findings.governingReading: a voice tinged with longing
findings.explanation: Saber’s wistful desire for an experience treated as unrepeatable becomes forward-looking hope.

findings.highlight: Everything can return to the way it was just like that.
findings.evidenceJa: それだけなら、まだ取り返しがつく筈だ
findings.governingReading: If he does only that, the situation should still be salvageable.
findings.explanation: A conditional belief that he can still avoid irreversible damage becomes certainty that everything will revert.

findings.highlight: I say something I won’t be able to take back.
findings.evidenceJa: おそらく、取り返しのつかなくなる言葉を口にした
findings.governingReading: He probably utters words that will make matters irreparable.
findings.explanation: The narrator’s おそらく uncertainty is removed.

findings.highlight: start fighting right now
findings.evidenceJa: この場で戦いに赴く
findings.governingReading: set out for battle from this very spot
findings.explanation: Saber’s readiness to depart immediately is changed into beginning combat at the bridge.

findings.highlight: you don’t like fighting
findings.evidenceJa: 自分から戦いたいなんて思ってないだろ
findings.governingReading: You do not actually wish to fight of your own accord.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s distinction between chosen desire and compelled action is reduced to whether Saber likes fighting.

findings.highlight: you could just attack people and take their power
findings.evidenceJa: ライダーみたいに人を襲って力を得ればいい
findings.governingReading: she could attack people to gain power as Rider did
findings.explanation: The concrete comparison to Rider’s conduct disappears, weakening the ethical and plot-specific example.

findings.highlight: she grits her teeth and straightens her stare
findings.evidenceJa: キッ、と歯を噛んで視線を正した
findings.governingReading: She clenches her teeth and sharply fixes her gaze.
findings.explanation: The sudden, forceful キッ marking Saber’s recovery and resistance disappears.

findings.highlight: But you still fear battles.
findings.evidenceJa: だけど、それでもおまえは戦いを嫌ってる
findings.governingReading: Even so, you hate or abhor battle.
findings.explanation: The translation repeats fear and erases Shirou’s distinct claim that Saber dislikes battle despite not fearing it.

findings.highlight: You must have hated even pulling out that sword.
findings.evidenceJa: 本当は剣を取る事さえ嫌だった筈だ
findings.governingReading: He claims she must originally have hated even taking up the sword.
findings.explanation: A life-defining acceptance of the sword and kingship is narrowed to drawing a weapon in combat.

findings.highlight: It’s so simple.
findings.evidenceJa: そんなことに
findings.governingReading: To such a thing—or to that truth about her.
findings.explanation: The fragment’s backward reference is replaced by an unsupported judgment that the issue is simple.

findings.highlight: glares at me in anger
findings.evidenceJa: 怒りをかみ殺して俺を睨む
findings.governingReading: She glares while biting back her anger.
findings.explanation: Saber’s active suppression and restraint disappear, leaving only expressed anger.

findings.highlight: She needs to regain the happiness she should have had as a human.
findings.evidenceJa: 本来掴むはずだった人間らしい幸福ってヤツを、今からでも取り戻せばいい
findings.governingReading: Even now, Saber should reclaim the human happiness she was meant to grasp.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s direct exhortation shifts into a detached third-person statement about what she needs.

findings.highlight: There are infinite ways!
findings.evidenceJa: 道なんていくらでもある
findings.governingReading: There are any number of paths open to her.
findings.explanation: The idiomatic abundance of possible lives is inflated into mathematical infinity.

findings.highlight: Don’t make any mistakes and don’t use the Holy Grail…
findings.evidenceJa: 間違っても。間違っても、聖杯を
findings.governingReading: Under no circumstances—under no circumstances use the Holy Grail…
findings.explanation: The repeated prohibitive idiom is mistranslated as advice not to make errors, breaking Shirou’s unfinished warning.

findings.highlight: She just looks back at me.
findings.evidenceJa: まっすぐに俺の目を見返して
findings.governingReading: She looks straight back into his eyes.
findings.explanation: Saber’s unwavering eye contact in refusing him is flattened.

findings.highlight: This wish has never changed
findings.evidenceJa: この誓いは永遠に変わらない
findings.governingReading: This oath will never change for all eternity.
findings.explanation: Saber’s binding oath is replaced by a personal wish, blurring duty, desire, and the Arthur/Arturia division.

findings.highlight: Our words end there.
findings.evidenceJa: そこで言葉は途切れた
findings.governingReading: His words break off there.
findings.explanation: The endpoint of Shirou’s attack is turned into a mutual end to speech even though Saber has remained silent.

findings.highlight: What makes you think you understand me?
findings.evidenceJa: 貴方程度の人間に、私の何が解るというのです
findings.governingReading: What could a person of your low degree understand about her?
findings.explanation: Saber’s deliberately cruel belittling of Shirou’s stature is omitted.

findings.highlight: You have no right to invade me.
findings.evidenceJa: 私に踏み入る権利などない
findings.governingReading: You have no right to intrude into her inner affairs or cross that boundary.
findings.explanation: An interpersonal boundary is rendered as an unnatural physical or sexualized invasion.

findings.highlight: What are you saying when you need me to protect you?
findings.evidenceJa: 私に守られなければならない未熟なマスターが何を
findings.governingReading: What right has an immature Master who must be protected by her to say this?
findings.explanation: The insult to Shirou’s immaturity and Master status disappears.

findings.highlight: you are even more mistaken
findings.evidenceJa: 貴方の方こそ何かを間違えている
findings.governingReading: You are the one who has something wrong.
findings.explanation: The reversal of accusation is turned into an unsupported comparative ranking of who is more wrong.

findings.highlight: Only corpses consider others more important than themselves.
findings.evidenceJa: 自身より他人を優先するなど死者の考えだ
findings.governingReading: Putting others before oneself is the thinking of a dead person.
findings.explanation: Saber’s diagnosis of Shirou’s death-oriented mentality becomes a universal claim about literal corpses.

findings.highlight: because I’m suppressing my emotion
findings.evidenceJa: 自分でも驚くほど、感情を押し殺している為だった
findings.governingReading: because he is suppressing his feelings to a degree that surprises even him
findings.explanation: The extraordinary degree of Shirou’s restraint and his surprise at it disappear.

findings.highlight: I bear my head going white
findings.evidenceJa: 目の前が真っ白になるのを堪えて
findings.governingReading: He fights through his vision going completely white.
findings.explanation: A visual blackout from shock becomes the nonsensical image of his head changing color.

findings.highlight: I get away from her.
findings.evidenceJa: 離れていく姿
findings.governingReading: Her figure recedes as he runs away.
findings.explanation: The visual image of Saber falling away from Shirou’s viewpoint becomes a statement of his successful escape.

findings.highlight: I keep running
findings.evidenceJa: 激情に任せて走った
findings.governingReading: He runs at the mercy of his violent emotion.
findings.explanation: The force governing Shirou’s uncontrolled flight disappears.

findings.highlight: It’s not just Saber that I’m mad at.
findings.evidenceJa: 頭にきているのはセイバーにじゃない
findings.governingReading: The person he is angry at is not Saber.
findings.explanation: The English says Saber remains one target of his anger, directly reversing his realization that the anger is aimed at himself.

findings.highlight: What was it about?
findings.evidenceJa: あれは、どんな吐露だったのか
findings.governingReading: What kind of emotional disclosure had that been?
findings.explanation: Shirou’s reassessment of Saber’s vulnerable outpouring becomes a vague question about topic.

findings.highlight: A voice of hope, disappointment, and wishes.
findings.evidenceJa: 期待と失望と、懇願の混じった声
findings.governingReading: A voice mingling expectation, disappointment, and pleading.
findings.explanation: The urgent plea in Saber’s voice is weakened into generic wishes, and expectation becomes hope.

findings.highlight: shut the door
findings.evidenceJa: ピシャリ、と障子を閉める
findings.governingReading: He snaps the shoji closed.
findings.explanation: The specific sliding screen and sharp action grounding the Emiya room disappear.

findings.highlight: I don’t want to do anything that might endanger it.
findings.evidenceJa: 自分から死ぬような真似はしたくない
findings.governingReading: He does not want deliberately to do something tantamount to dying.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s narrow defensive claim that he does not seek death is broadened into avoiding danger, contradicting his repeated risk-taking.

findings.highlight: if she denies me like that
findings.evidenceJa: それをあんな風に否定されたら
findings.governingReading: if that claim is rejected in that fashion
findings.explanation: Saber’s rejection of Shirou’s proposition becomes a rejection of Shirou himself.

findings.highlight: I’ll be seriously hurt.
findings.evidenceJa: 取り返しのつかないぐらいのダメージ
findings.governingReading: damage beyond repair
findings.explanation: The irreversible emotional damage he realizes he already bears is reduced to unspecified serious hurt.

findings.highlight: had sex with her even though it was just to survive. saw into the depths of her heart to survive.
findings.evidenceJa: 心の深部を重ね見た
findings.governingReading: To survive, their views overlapped into the depths of each other’s hearts.
findings.explanation: A sexually explicit interpretive variant is printed before a second translation of the same clause, leaving unsupported content and duplicate revisions in the live text.

findings.highlight: The heat of that night wasn’t a burn, but it almost killed my brain.
findings.evidenceJa: あの熱さ。あいつの深層にあった光を思い出す
findings.governingReading: He remembers that heat and the light within Saber’s depths.
findings.explanation: mirror moon inserts an unsupported near-fatal brain injury and a coarse emotional gloss, then repeats the source-faithful memory sequence after the abandoned variant.
